questions.statement: Which sentence uses the past continuous correctly?

options.text: While I studied, the phone was ringing.
options.feedback: 'Was ringing' makes the interruption the ongoing action, which reverses the roles.

options.text: While I study, the phone rang.
options.feedback: 'Study' would need the past simple to match a past 'rang'.

options.text: While I was studying, the phone rang.
options.feedback: 'Was studying' sets the action in progress and 'rang' interrupts it.

options.text: While I was study, the phone rang.
options.feedback: 'Was study' is not a valid past continuous form.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo describe una accion en curso en un momento del pasado. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'We ____ TV at nine when the power went out.'
questions.context: Past continuous en contexto, Ponce, grado 11.

options.text: watched
options.feedback: The simple past would place the action as a completed event, not as background.

options.text: were watching
options.feedback: 'Were watching' is the past continuous of 'watch'.

options.text: have watched
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to that past moment.

options.text: are watching
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to now, not to the past.

questions.explanation:
La accion en curso en ese momento del pasado va en pasado continuo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does the past continuous express when it is interrupted?

options.text: The longer background action that the shorter action interrupts
options.feedback: This is the classic interrupted-action pattern.

options.text: The shorter action that interrupts the longer one
options.feedback: The roles are reversed: the continuous is the background.

options.text: Two actions completed at the same time
options.feedback: Two simple past actions would be needed for that reading.

options.text: A habit in the past
options.feedback: Habits require 'used to' plus the base form.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo marca la accion larga de fondo y el pasado simple la accion corta que la interrumpe.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: 'I ____ my homework when my friend called me.'

options.text: did
options.feedback: 'Did' is the simple past and would mark a completed action.

options.text: was doing
options.feedback: 'Was doing' is the past continuous of 'do'.

options.text: do
options.feedback: The bare form would need an auxiliary.

options.text: have done
options.feedback: The present perfect refers to the present, not to the past.

questions.explanation:
La accion que ya estaba ocurriendo cuando llego la llamada va en pasado continuo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: She is reading when her phone rang.
options.feedback: The present continuous would conflict with the past 'rang'.

options.text: She read when her phone was ringing.
options.feedback: This reverses the background and interrupting actions.

options.text: She was reading when her phone rang.
options.feedback: The pattern is past continuous plus 'when' plus simple past.

options.text: She was reading while her phone rang.
options.feedback: 'While' needs both clauses in the continuous for simultaneity.

questions.explanation:
La oracion correcta combina el pasado continuo con un conector temporal y el pasado simple.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'They were playing football at 5 p.m. and then they stopped.' What does 'were playing' tell us?
questions.context: Analisis de la accion en curso, Carolina, grado 11.

options.text: The action was in progress at that hour
options.feedback: The past continuous fixes a moment with the action ongoing.

options.text: The action started exactly at five
options.feedback: The start of the action is not stated by the continuous.

options.text: The action finished at five
options.feedback: 'Stopped' marks the end, not the continuous itself.

options.text: The action was repeated daily
options.feedback: Repetition would need 'every day' or a similar marker.

questions.explanation:
Indica que la accion estaba en curso a las cinco y termino mas tarde. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the preposition that correctly introduces the interruption: 'He fell ____ he was climbing the wall.'

options.text: during
options.feedback: 'During' marks a period and cannot introduce this clause.

options.text: since
options.feedback: 'Since' marks an origin in time, not a background action.

options.text: while
options.feedback: 'While' introduces the background action of the past continuous.

options.text: until
options.feedback: 'Until' marks an endpoint and would reverse the meaning.

questions.explanation:
'While' introduce la accion de fondo y 'as soon as' la interrupcion en el instante exacto.

questions.statement: Complete: 'At eight o'clock I ____ dinner when the lights went off.'

options.text: had
options.feedback: 'Had' would be the simple past and would mark a completed action.

options.text: was having
options.feedback: 'Was having' is the past continuous of 'have' in this sense.

options.text: have
options.feedback: The bare form requires an auxiliary.

options.text: am having
options.feedback: The present continuous refers to the present.

questions.explanation:
La cena ya estaba en curso a las ocho cuando ocurrio el corte de luz. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses two past continuous actions correctly?

options.text: While she was cooking, her brother was setting the table.
options.feedback: Both actions are simultaneous and both use the continuous.

options.text: While she was cooking, her brother set the table.
options.feedback: The simple past turns the second action into an interruption.

options.text: While she is cooking, her brother was setting the table.
options.feedback: A present continuous would clash with the past tense.

options.text: While she was cooking, her brother has set the table.
options.feedback: The present perfect would link the second action to the present.

questions.explanation:
Dos acciones en curso al mismo tiempo se expresan ambas en pasado continuo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read the text: 'I was walking home when a car stopped beside me.' What happened first?
questions.context: Orden de acciones, Vega Baja, grado 11.

options.text: The walk had already started
options.feedback: The past continuous gives the background action that was running.

options.text: The car stopped first
options.feedback: The sentence presents the walk as the ongoing action and the car as the interruption.

options.text: Both began at the same moment
options.feedback: Nothing in the sentence marks a simultaneous beginning.

options.text: The walk started after the car stopped
options.feedback: That would be the reverse of the information given.

questions.explanation:
El camino a casa ya estaba en curso cuando el coche se detuvo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence correctly uses the past continuous with 'while'?

options.text: While the baby will sleep, the phone rang.
options.feedback: 'Will' cannot be used in a past background clause.

options.text: While the baby sleeps, the phone rang.
options.feedback: The present continuous would not match a past interruption.

options.text: While the baby slept, the phone rang.
options.feedback: 'Slept' is the short background action interrupted by 'rang'.

options.text: While the baby slept, the phone rang yesterday again.
options.feedback: The trailing 'yesterday again' adds nothing coherent.

questions.explanation:
'While' se usa con acciones simultaneas; el pasado continuo encaja con esa relacion.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Look at the sentence: 'We were play tennis when it started to rain.' What is the error?

options.text: Nothing is wrong with the sentence
options.feedback: The missing -ing makes the sentence ungrammatical.

options.text: 'Rained' must be 'raining'
options.feedback: 'Rained' is correct for the interrupting action.

options.text: 'We' must be 'They'
options.feedback: The subject agrees with the rest of the sentence.

options.text: 'Were play' must be 'were playing'
options.feedback: The past continuous always requires the -ing form.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo exige la forma con 'ing': 'were playing'. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What is the difference between 'I was reading' and 'I read'?

options.text: Both mean exactly the same thing
options.feedback: The two tenses differ in aspect, not merely in style.

options.text: The continuous refers to the present
options.feedback: It refers to a moment in the past.

options.text: The simple past is used only in questions
options.feedback: It is used in statements, questions and negatives alike.

options.text: The continuous shows an action in progress; the simple shows a completed event
options.feedback: The continuous carries the background and duration reading.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo muestra la accion como parte de un fondo en curso; el pasado simple la presenta como un hecho ponctual.

questions.statement: Which sentence describes an action that started in the past and continued into another past moment?
questions.context: Duracion en el pasado, Barceloneta, grado 11.

options.text: They were living in Ponce while their children were studying in Mayaguez
options.feedback: Both prolonged situations are expressed in the past continuous.

options.text: They lived in Ponce while their children studied in Mayaguez
options.feedback: Two simple pasts lose the sense of ongoing duration.

options.text: They are living in Ponce while their children study in Mayaguez
options.feedback: The present continuous would refer to current, not past, situations.

options.text: They have lived in Ponce while their children have studied in Mayaguez
options.feedback: The present perfect would link both facts to the present.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo encaja con acciones extendidas que coexisten en el pasado. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.context: Past continuous con 'by the time', Maunabo, grado 11.

options.text: already started

options.text: has already started

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does 'as' mean in the sentence 'She dropped the book as she fell'?

options.text: One action happened long before the other
options.feedback: That would be the reading of 'after' or 'by the time'.

options.text: One action caused the other
options.feedback: Causation requires 'because' or 'so'.

options.text: One action happened every day
options.feedback: Repetition would need 'every time'.

options.text: Both actions happened at the same time
options.feedback: 'As' marks simultaneity between two past events.

questions.explanation:
'As' indica que ambas acciones ocurrieron al mismo tiempo. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?
questions.context: Revision del pasado continuo, Toa Baja, grado 11.

options.text: I was tired and I was sleeping early.
options.feedback: Both clauses can be in the past continuous with no conflict.

options.text: I was sleeping while I slept.
options.feedback: The same subject cannot sleep twice at once in two tenses.

options.text: I was tired and I slept early.
options.feedback: That combination of continuous and simple past is also valid.

options.text: I was sleeping while she was working.
options.feedback: Two different subjects in the continuous cause no conflict.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo no puede usarse con el pasado simple en la misma oracion para el mismo sujeto.

questions.statement: Choose the sentence that best describes two overlapping past activities.

options.text: She revised for the test while her friends were partying next door
options.feedback: The simple past would make her revision a bounded event.

options.text: She will revise for the test while her friends were partying next door
options.feedback: A future clause cannot overlap a past clause in that way.

options.text: She was revising for the test while her friends were partying next door
options.feedback: Two simultaneous background activities, both in the continuous.

options.text: She has revised for the test while her friends party next door
options.feedback: The present perfect and present simple refer to the present.

questions.explanation:
El pasado continuo en ambas clausulas expresa dos actividades simultaneas. Es uno de los puntos mas frecuentes de las pruebas de esta unidad.
